title: A separating coproduct gives an epimorphism from a coproduct of its summands
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with sets as Hom-sets, and let $(G_b)_{b\in B}$ be a family of objects of $\mathcal C$ indexed by a set $B$ whose coproduct $\coprod_{b\in B}G_b$ exists in $\mathcal C$ and is a *separator* of $\mathcal C$: for every two morphisms $u\neq v:M\to N$ of $\mathcal C$ there is a morphism $h:\coprod_bG_b\to M$ with $u h\neq v h$. Let $A$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, let $I_A$ be the set of pairs $(Y,h)$ with $Y$ an object of $\mathcal C$ equal to $G_b$ for some $b\in B$ and $h:Y\to A$ a morphism, and suppose that the coproduct $\coprod_{(Y,h)\in I_A}Y$ exists in $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then the morphism $\coprod_{(Y,h)\in I_A}Y\to A$ whose restriction to the summand indexed by $(Y,h)$ is $h$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal C$.
